Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisisBy Barbara Angopa and APPublished On 6 Nov 20266 Nov 2026
Paraguay’s President Santiago Pena is facing impeachment following the collapse of Ueno Bank, a major digital bank, which has plunged the South American country into its deepest political crisis in more than a decade.
Pena announced his resignation on Thursday, but politicians formally filed impeachment charges against the president. Pena, a former International Monetary Fund (IMF) economist, then requested a 72-hour extension to present his defence at an impeachment hearing, because he had been given less than 12 hours to answer “an accusatory writ and about 300 pages of attachments”, adding: “That is not due process.”
Recommended Stories list of 1 itemlist 1 of 1Paraguay bank collapses with half of population’s savingsend of list
However, the Senate convened a rare session on Friday to consider Pena’s political future, opting to move forward with efforts to remove him from office.
Until March 2025, Pena held a stake in Grupo Vazquez, the parent company that owns Ueno Bank.
What is Ueno Bank?
Ueno Bank was established in 1976 and remained a small financial operation for decades.
After being granted a full banking licence in 2023, it rebranded and grew to become a household name in Paraguay within five years. Customers were incentivised with cashback offers on groceries and it built a network of more than 70 branches. The bank sponsored Paraguay’s national football team and its name was plastered across the country’s main stadium.
Ueno bank reported that it had 3 million customers, roughly 60 percent of Paraguay’s adult population.

Why is Paraguay facing a banking and political crisis?By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 6 Nov 20266 Nov 2026
Lawmakers in Paraguay have resumed impeachment proceedings against President Santiago Pena, a day after he resigned amid links to the country’s worst financial crisis in decades.
The Senate convened a rare session on Friday to consider Pena’s political future, opting to move forward with efforts to remove the conservative economist from office.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Paraguay bank collapses with half of population’s savingslist 2 of 3Paraguay Congress rejects President Pena’s resignation after bank collapselist 3 of 3Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisisend of list
Politicians formally filed impeachment charges against the president on Thursday, despite his resignation. Pena, who was elected in 2023, has requested a 72-hour extension to prepare his defence before the Senate.
The proceedings follow a vote in Paraguay’s lower house of Congress, where lawmakers overwhelmingly approved impeachment charges against Pena in a 78-0 vote.
The political turmoil surrounding the country’s president follows Paraguay’s central bank’s intervention earlier this week at Ueno Bank, one of the country’s fastest-growing digital lenders, citing breaches of minimum solvency requirements.
Pena previously held a stake in Ueno’s parent company, Grupo Vazquez, until last year, when he claims he sold his shares. Paraguayan lawmakers have accused the president of a conflict of interest and questioned whether authorities failed to act on warnings about the lender’s financial position.

Taiwan has formal diplomatic ties with only three Pacific Islands nations: Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands [File: Ritchie B. Tongo/EPA]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and ReutersPublished On 6 Nov 20266 Nov 2026
Taiwan says it is closing its representative office in Papua New Guinea and will stop buying liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the country, blaming Chinese political pressure on the South Pacific nation.
Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Friday that Papua New Guinea had repeated previous demands that staff leave its office in the capital, Port Moresby, within a set deadline and had pushed for ⁠its closure.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Trump praises US-China friendship at state dinner with Xi Jinpinglist 2 of 3‘Hybrid warfare’: Taiwan drives away 16 Chinese shipslist 3 of 3Kylian Mbappe loses Chinese sponsors for calling Mao ‘Chinese dictator’end of list
These actions “reflect China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries’ diplomatic decisions and suppress Taiwan’s international space”, it said in a statement.
China, which claims Taiwan as part of its territory, had welcomed Papua New Guinea’s decision in July to shutter Taiwan’s office in Port Moresby. Taipei rejected the move, and the office remained open in the interim.
The Pacific has long been an area for diplomatic competition between China and Taiwan. Papua New Guinea has formal diplomatic relations with China, but it had allowed Taiwan to have a representative office in Port Moresby.

A resident of Omdurman carries water in a container as he heads home with his children amid Sudan's war [File: El Tayeb Siddig/Sudan]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 6 Nov 20266 Nov 2026
Millions of people in Sudan who have been displaced by the country’s civil war risk being left ⁠without emergency shelter due to funding shortages and depleting aid stocks, according to the United Nations refugee agency and the International Organization for Migration.
An ⁠estimated 15.4 million people across Sudan urgently need emergency shelter and basic household items, but funding shortages mean humanitarian agencies can prioritise assistance for only approximately 10 percent of those in need, the two UN agencies said in a joint statement on Friday.

So far, only 936,000 people have received assistance, leaving a large ‌gap between needs and available resources, according to the statement.
